subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress sub-agent announce

question: Should OpenClaw expose a public per-spawn completion-delivery control that can deterministically suppress the requester handoff, and should any global default be added now?
rationale: The direct bypass has already been addressed, while the remaining request creates a new tool/config contract with consequences for orchestration, user expectations, cleanup, and retries; source evidence does not establish a maintainer-approved permanent API direction.

options.title: Add per-spawn skip only
options.body: Define a narrow additive `sessions_spawn` mode that suppresses requester completion delivery while preserving current default behavior and defer any persistent config default.

options.title: Add routing modes together
options.body: Adopt a broader public completion-delivery contract that includes requester, parent, and skip destinations, with explicit lifecycle semantics.

options.title: Keep model-directed behavior
options.body: Decline a framework control and retain the existing requester-agent handoff plus model-output suppression tokens.

recommendation.title: Add per-spawn skip only
recommendation.body: Define a narrow additive `sessions_spawn` mode that suppresses requester completion delivery while preserving current default behavior and defer any persistent config default.

likelyOwner.reason: History in the preceding current-main review connects Peter most directly to `sessions_spawn` and the current announce/delivery implementation.
